newsitem.title: JAPAN: Electronic glitch sends Tokyo stocks tumbling.
newsitem.headline: Electronic glitch sends Tokyo stocks tumbling.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange suffered its worst ever technical glitch on Friday when its electronic trading system crashed, setting off a flurry of sales that sent the key index plunging to one of its biggest losses this year.
The trading system was out for the entire two-hour morning session, halting trade in more than 1,700 issues, 108 of them on the benchmark Nikkei 225 average.

With only the 150 floor-traded issues to trade, most market participants sat out the morning session. But when trading resumed after the lunch break, the shower of arbitrage-linked sales that emerged sent the Nikkei 225 down 527.05 points, or nearly three percent, to close at 19,804.38.
It was its first close below 20,000 since July 1l and its sixth-biggest points loss this year.
"The fall in futures accelerated after the release of glum domestic July car sales data," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities.
The bourse said it still had to figure out what went wrong.
"We would like to apologise to investors for the trouble," a TSE official told reporters. "We have not yet figured out what was behind the system breakdown. We will investigate the case," he said.
He said there was no problem in the system hardware and that the breakdown may have been caused by a software malfunction.
He said the bourse would try to prevent any repeat of such a system failure, but when asked if the bourse would take specific steps to improve its back-up system, he replied:
"I think it would be difficult to make any drastic overhaul of the system."

Unlike in October 1990, when a problem with cables halted trade, this time the electronic trading system itself crashed, the first time this has happened. It was the worst mishap since the system was introduced in 1982, the bourse said.

The failure could not have come at a worse time for the bourse, which has recently been hit by a high-profile scandal involving payoffs to racketeers by big brokerages that has caused individual investors to shy away from stock trading.
The TSE official said there was no framework at the moment to compensate losses arising from a trading system breakdown.
"The failure threw everyone off in the morning session and unleashed arbitrage-linked selling after trade resumed," said Mitsuru Hayashino, general manager at Sanyo Securities.

A total of 724 issues of system-traded convertible bonds and two warrant issues were suspended, along with system-traded stock options for four individual issues: Denso Corp, Dai Nippon Printing Co, Seven-Eleven Japan Co and Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd.
Morning turnover shrank to a meagre 123 million shares, down from the 221 million shares traded on Thursday morning.
By the end of the day turnover was 450 million shares, little changed from Thursday, but losers overwhelmed winners 944 to 184.
